# G8.1 — HotChocolate profiled: the phase that does not terminate inside 600s is NAMED

**Date** 2026-07-29 · **Branch** `feat/graph-v2` · **Session** s24 · **Checkpoint** G8.1

**Answer in one line:** the phase is **`GenericExtraction`**, and inside it the single extractor
**`SyntaxStructureExtractor`** — **95.4 %** of the whole analysis — whose `ResolveTypeDeclaration` is
**quadratic within one file**. HotChocolate contains **one 11.3 MB generated file** that alone costs
**20 min 17 s** of a **21 min 15 s** run.

The wall is **not** "HotChocolate is a big repo". Without that extractor's cost the same repo — all
8,658 files, 343 projects, 33 solutions — analyses in **≈58 seconds**.

---

## 0. The instrument had to be built first

Neither existing CLI observer can profile a hang, because both report a hang **as silence**:

| Instrument | Behaviour under redirected stdout | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| `SpectreDiscoveryObserver` (default non-interactive) | `WriteLine` enqueues to its buffer and **returns before the console write** when `!Interactive` (`SpectreDiscoveryObserver.cs:123`) — a run that never ends prints nothing | `todoapi-trace.txt`: 83 lines, all map output, zero stage lines |
| `WaterfallDiscoveryObserver` (`DEVCONTEXT_WATERFALL=on`) | Spectre `Progress` fallback emits percentage rows, no elapsed, only on task completion | `todoapi-waterfall.txt`: 3 progress lines, all `0%` |
| `--trace` (Serilog `Debug`) | the pipeline logs no stage events at all | `todoapi-trace.txt`: nothing |

So S5 could only ever report *"produced no dump in 28 minutes"* — it had no way to see **where**.

**New:** `src/DevContext.Cli/Observers/ProfileDiscoveryObserver.cs` — gated on `DEVCONTEXT_PROFILE=1`,
streams one line **per lifecycle event to stderr the moment it happens**, plus a `HEARTBEAT` every
`DEVCONTEXT_PROFILE_HEARTBEAT_SEC` seconds naming the stage in flight and the extractors still
outstanding. Kill the process at any point and the log still names the phase. Off by default, and on
stderr, so every harness's captured stdout stays byte-stable.

Verified on a pole that finishes before it was pointed at one that does not — `todoapi-profile.txt`,
full waterfall, `PIPELINE-DONE` at T+1.9s.

---

## 1. The run — per-phase timings, real repo, harness arguments

```
DEVCONTEXT_PROFILE=1 DEVCONTEXT_PROFILE_HEARTBEAT_SEC=10 \
  DevContext.Cli.exe analyze C:/code/DevContext2/eval-repos/HotChocolate -o …kernel.json --format json
```

(the same argument shape `eval/graph-truth.ps1:163` uses for this pole — positional path, no `--sln`)

Full stream: **`hotchocolate-profile.txt`**. Condensed:

| T+ | event |
|---|---|
| 0.0s | `PIPELINE-START` |
| 0.9s | `FileTreeExtractor` done — 838 ms |
| 1.1s | `SolutionDiscovery` done — 253 ms |
| 6.3s | `ProjectStructure` done — 5,147 ms |
| 6.3s | **`STAGE-DONE DiscoveryAndCacheWarmup` — 6,256 ms** |
| 6.3s | **`STAGE-START GenericExtraction`** |
| 6.3s | `LayerClassifier` done — 15 ms |
| 6.5s | `DependencyExtractor` done — 243 ms |
| 38.4s | `ProgramCsFlowExtractor` done — 32,101 ms |
| 39.9s | `DiRegistrationExtractor` done — 33,640 ms |
| 40.0s → | `HEARTBEAT stage=GenericExtraction running=1:SyntaxStructureExtractor` — **every heartbeat from here on** |
| **600s** | **budget expires** — the line at exactly that mark reads<br>`[profile] T+   600.0s HEARTBEAT stage=GenericExtraction running=1:SyntaxStructureExtractor` |
| 1223.3s | `SyntaxStructureExtractor` done — **1,216,998 ms (20 min 17 s)**, +19,456 types |
| 1223.3s | **`STAGE-DONE GenericExtraction` — 1,217,002 ms** |
| 1272.7s | `PIPELINE-DONE` — types 19,456, detections 3,889 |
| 1275.1s | process exits, **total 21 min 15 s** |

**The 600s budget expires inside the FIRST heavy stage** — the line at that mark is a heartbeat, not
a transition. The run was allowed to continue past it (for the profile only — the budget itself was
not touched) and it does eventually finish, which lets the whole pipeline be weighed:

| stage | elapsed | share |
|---|---|---|
| `DiscoveryAndCacheWarmup` | 6,256 ms | 0.5 % |
| **`GenericExtraction`** | **1,217,002 ms** | **95.4 %** |
| `SignalSealing` | 1 ms | — |
| `SpecificExtraction` | 10,873 ms | 0.9 % |
| `SemanticLite` | 27,624 ms | 2.2 % |
| `GraphAssembly` | 7,133 ms | 0.6 % |
| `Insights` | 975 ms | 0.1 % |
| `Compression` | 1,762 ms | 0.1 % |
| `Snapshot` | 843 ms | 0.1 % |
| **total** | **1,275 s** | |

and inside `GenericExtraction`, `SyntaxStructureExtractor` is **1,216,998 ms of 1,217,002 ms**. Every
other extractor in the stage finished by T+40s.

**So: strip that one extractor's cost and HotChocolate analyses in ≈58 seconds** — comfortably
inside the 600s budget, between PowerToys (83 s) and bitwarden-server (214 s), exactly where a repo
of its size belongs. There is **no second wall**: `SemanticLite` builds a Roslyn compilation over all
8,658 trees *including* the 11 MB one in 27.6 s.

## 2. The method — `dotnet-stack`, two samples, identical

`hc-stack-sample1.txt`, `hc-stack-sample2.txt`. In both, exactly **one** thread carries `CPU_TIME`
and it is the same stack (every other thread is parked in `LowLevelLifoSemaphore.Wait`):

```
CPU_TIME
  Microsoft.CodeAnalysis!SyntaxNode+<DescendantNodesOnly>d__175.MoveNext()
  System.Linq!Enumerable+OfTypeIterator`1.MoveNext()
  System.Linq!Enumerable.FirstOrDefault(...)
  DevContext.Core!SyntaxStructureExtractor.ResolveTypeDeclaration(BaseTypeSyntax)
  DevContext.Core!SyntaxStructureExtractor.<ExtractInterfaces>b__17_0(BaseTypeSyntax)
  DevContext.Core!SyntaxStructureExtractor.ExtractInterfaces(TypeDeclarationSyntax)
  DevContext.Core!SyntaxStructureExtractor.CreateTypeDiscovery(TypeDeclarationSyntax, String)
  DevContext.Core!SyntaxStructureExtractor.<ExtractAsync>b__2  ← the per-file task
```

## 3. The algorithm — `SyntaxStructureExtractor.cs:342-353`

```csharp
private static BaseTypeDeclarationSyntax? ResolveTypeDeclaration(BaseTypeSyntax baseType)
{
    var typeName = baseType.Type.ToString();
    var root = baseType.SyntaxTree.GetCompilationUnitRoot();
    var candidate = root.DescendantNodes()                       // ← whole file, every time
        .OfType<BaseTypeDeclarationSyntax>()
        .FirstOrDefault(t => t.Identifier.ValueText == typeName
            || typeName.StartsWith(t.Identifier.ValueText + "<", StringComparison.Ordinal));
    return candidate;
}
```

Three compounding properties:

1. **A full syntax-tree walk per base-list entry.** Cost is
   `O(typesInFile × baseEntriesPerType × nodesInFile)` — **quadratic inside a single file**, so it is
   bounded by the largest *file*, not by repo size.
2. **Called twice per entry.** `ExtractBaseTypes` (`:308`) and `ExtractInterfaces` (`:319`) each build
   the same `(TypeName, Declaration)` tuple independently and throw the other half away.
3. **No early exit on the common case.** The key is `baseType.Type.ToString()`, so a qualified base
   such as `global::System.IEquatable<Foo>` matches **no** declaration and `FirstOrDefault` runs to
   the end of the tree.

## 4. The input — one file, 43× larger than anything else in the repo

| | HotChocolate | OrchardCore | bitwarden-server | PowerToys |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `.cs` files | 8,658 | 5,247 | 4,927 | 3,800 |
| `.csproj` | 343 | 233 | 64 | 208 |
| solutions on disk | 33 (**none at repo root**) | 1 | 1 | 12 |
| C# source | 47 MB | 10 MB | 63 MB | 16 MB |
| analyze | **TIMEOUT** | finishes | 214 s (S5) | 83 s (S5) |

File-count and even byte-count fail to separate it — bitwarden carries *more* C# and finishes in
214 s. The distribution does:

```
src/Nitro/Common/src/ChilliCream.Nitro.Client/Generated/ApiClient.Client.cs   11,340,604 bytes
…/CodeGeneration.CSharp.Tests/Integration/StarWarsIntrospectionTest.Client.cs    259,821 bytes   ← next largest
```

That one file — a StrawberryShake-generated GraphQL client, first line `// <auto-generated/>` —
holds **240,772 lines, 5,455 type declarations, 4,598 base lists**, and its base lists are exactly
the pathological shape:

```csharp
public partial class CreateMockSchemaResult
    : global::System.IEquatable<CreateMockSchemaResult>, ICreateMockSchemaResult
```

≈ 9,200 base entries × 2 calls ≈ **18,400 full walks of a 240k-line tree**, most with no early exit.

## 5. The quadratic, measured — isolation experiment

The file was copied into scratch single-project repos **outside** the repo
(`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\g8-scale\fracNN`), cut at exact type boundaries so each stays valid C#. One
`.csproj`, one `.cs`, nothing else. Real `analyze --no-cache` on each:

| fraction | lines | types | `SyntaxStructureExtractor` | growth vs previous |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 12 % | 28,892 | 820 | 22,180 ms | — |
| 25 % | 60,151 | 1,743 | 95,198 ms | **×4.29** for ×2.08 input |
| 50 % | 120,381 | 3,781 | 361,483 ms | **×3.80** for ×2.00 input |
| 100 % | 240,772 | 5,408 | **1,216,998 ms = 20 min 17 s** (measured on the full repo, §1) | ×3.37 |

**≈×4 per doubling is O(n²)**, read off the wall clock rather than off the source. The last row is
the full-repo run's own number, so it also carries every *other* file in HotChocolate; its ratio is
the low one because the 50 % run was the contended one (see caveat below), which inflates the
denominator. And **20 minutes for one file** lands on S5's observation — *"produced no dump in 28
minutes"* — almost exactly.

The rest of the pipeline is not implicated: in the 25 % run, `SyntaxStructureExtractor` is
**95.2 s of a 97.5 s** total (97.6 %); `SemanticLite`, `GraphAssembly`, `Insights`, `Compression`
and `Snapshot` together cost 2.3 s.

Artifacts: `scale-frac12.txt`, `scale-frac25.txt`, `scale-frac50.txt`.

*Honest caveat:* the fraction runs shared the machine with the live full-repo run. Both are
single-threaded at the bottleneck and the box has 8 cores, so the ratios — which are the claim — are
unaffected; the absolute full-repo T+ values after ~T+400s are slightly inflated.

## 6. The defect class, named (this is what R1's exit criterion asks for)

> **A single pathological file makes analysis unbounded.** Extraction cost is quadratic *within one
> file*, so no amount of repo-level scoping, project filtering or parallelism bounds it — one
> machine-generated source file is enough to exceed any budget, on a repo that is otherwise ordinary.

It is a **new class**, not a bigger instance of an existing one: the poles that finish are not
smaller in files or bytes, they simply have no single file like this one.

Filed as **bug #21**. G8.2 decides fix vs accepted limitation — **not** by raising the timeout.
